reviewer_role: Author; personally read all complete actual source units, every proposed target and necessary context, then separately reread every complete source-target-category-rationale triple before freeze.
review_method: Freshly read all 134 complete actual source units in chapters 15–19 with complete_text (29/42/27/17/19), then all proposed targets and their necessary narrative, grammatical, legal, and speaker context. Separately reread every complete source/target/category/rationale triple in unclipped draft batches 1–39, 40–79, 80–119, 120–154, and 155–176. Preserved the immutable original draft and exact before/after refinement artifacts. Seven exact refinements comprise five rationale clarifications, one stronger freshly read target replacement, and removal of one redundant overlapping Samuel target; the six changed retained triples were then separately reread in full. The final 175 retained pairs concern all 134 actual sources; a target range counts once. Reading extra context adds no completion credit. This is a curated supplied-English review, not exhaustive discovery, an original-language or apparatus review, numerical harmonization, or an independent equation of differently spelled names.
pin_method: Freshly fetched all thirteen used books from the exact immutable raw source commit. Verified every complete raw Git blob SHA1 against that commit’s previously recorded source-checks registry, saved separate author raw files and SHA256 hashes, and verified full parsed equality to the local source cache. Rehashed all saved raw files and rechecked full cache equality at freeze. All used books already had registry metadata; no guessed blob or new metadata lookup was used.

old_row.rationale: The resumed ascent from Abdedom’s house follows the earlier interruption in which the ark stayed three months in the house named Abeddara and God blessed the householder. The two forms are retained within the consecutive ark narrative.

new_row.rationale: The resumed ascent from Abdedom’s house follows the earlier interruption in which the ark stayed three months in the house named Abeddara and God blessed Abeddaram. All three source forms remain distinct within the consecutive ark narrative.

changes.reason: Name all three actual forms rather than call them two forms.

old_row.rationale: The song links the Abrahamic covenant and Isaac’s oath; God’s promise to Isaac in Genesis explicitly establishes the oath sworn to Abraham and promises the land to Isaac and his seed.

new_row.rationale: The song links the covenant with Abraham and God’s oath to Isaac; God’s promise to Isaac in Genesis explicitly establishes the oath sworn to Abraham and promises the land to Isaac and his seed.

changes.reason: Clarify that God gives the oath to Isaac; Isaac is not its speaker.

old_row.rationale: David’s return to bless his household is the point at which Samuel narrates the exchange with Saul’s daughter and its closing childlessness notice; Chronicles ends the scene before that exchange.

changes.reason: Remove a second overlapping Samuel target: the retained 6:19-20 already supplies the particular departure and household-blessing parallel; the further dispute is extra context and earns no second pair credit.

old_row.rationale: David contrasts his cedar house with the ark’s temporary shelter before Nathan in both accounts; Chronicles says beneath skins, while Samuel calls it the tent and adds rest from surrounding enemies.

new_row.rationale: David contrasts his cedar house with the ark’s temporary shelter before Nathan in both accounts; Chronicles says beneath skins, while Samuel calls it the tent and adds possession on every side away from surrounding enemies.

changes.reason: Preserve Samuel’s actual possession wording instead of paraphrasing it as rest.

old_row.rationale: Both prayers combine the Lord Almighty and God of Israel titles with the enduring word concerning David’s house and God’s glorified name; Chronicles explicitly asks that the house stand upright before Him.

new_row.rationale: Both prayers invoke the Lord Almighty, God of Israel, in connection with His word about David’s house; Chronicles asks that the house stand upright, while Samuel asks confirmation of the word and magnification of God’s name.

changes.reason: Distinguish the source’s divine titles and upright house from the target’s explicit magnification of the name.

old_row.rationale: David’s consecration of captured silver and gold belongs to his broader account of preparing abundance for God’s house and acknowledging that all of it comes from God’s hand; the later prayer does not enumerate these particular spoils.

new_row.rationale: David consecrates silver and gold taken from the nations; the later treasury notice explicitly includes holy things consecrated by David and gifts taken from wars and spoils for the building of God’s house. It does not identify every item in this campaign list individually.

changes.reason: Replace a broad gift-preparation comparison with the explicit Davidic war-spoil dedication and treasury notice, freshly read in full with context.

old_row.rationale: Both follow the messengers’ shaming with Ammon hiring Syrian aid. Chronicles specifies a thousand talents and chariots and horsemen from its named regions; Samuel lists foot-soldier contingents and different regional wording.

new_row.rationale: Both follow the messengers’ shaming with Ammon hiring Syrian aid. Chronicles specifies a thousand talents and chariots and horsemen from its named regions; Samuel lists twenty thousand foot soldiers and additional numbered groups of men, with different regional wording.

changes.reason: Do not make Samuel’s remaining unspecified men into foot soldiers.

editorial_notes: Chapter 16 has forty-two actual units, with no verse 24; the missing label was neither invented nor silently renumbered.

Psalms references were located and read from this pinned edition: the song parallels are Psalms 104, 95, and 105, and the Davidic psalms are 77 and 88. Familiar alternate numbering was not substituted.

Meaningful same-chapter links explicitly identify roster headings, grammatical antecedents, assignments, performance of instructions, or prayer answering its preceding oracle; every such link is labelled same-chapter.
Kaath, Hebron, Oziel, and Merari connections concern named ancestral branches or family ministries. Other names are not equated by phonetic similarity.
The ark narratives retain seven calves and seven rams versus a calf and a lamb, distinctive robe versus fine linen, different instrument lists, and Abdedom/Abeddara/Abeddaram/Obed-edom forms.
The supplied 2 Samuel 7:11 says that David will build God a house, unlike 1 Chronicles 17:10; the difference is explicitly retained, and the latter is also connected to its own prayer in 17:25.
Royal-sonship wording in Hebrews and the perpetual Davidic throne in Luke are identified as later christological reception without erasing the immediate successor and temple-building context.
Campaign comparisons retain different place names, actors, royal staff roles, golden collars versus armlets, horses versus horsemen, and the actual differing chariot and casualty figures.
One redundant second target for 16:43 was removed without source-credit loss. A broad comparison for 18:11 was replaced with the explicit war-spoil treasury notice in 26:26-27.
